question: Why did Francesca Moy's three former clients return to AEVS after working with other agencies?
transcript_excerpt: The three former clients returned to AEVS because they realized they were oversold on a cheaper solution that lacked proper support. episode_title: Fire the Chef: How Systems Save Your Client Experience| EPISODE 238
question: What does 'fire the chef' mean as a business system principle according to Francesca Moy?
transcript_excerpt: The principle means that a business should find a great chef or expert, document their recipe or process, then remove dependency on that individual by creating a standardized system everyone can follow. This ensures consistency regardless of which team member delivers the service or how they feel that day. Francesca implemented this at AEVS, resulting in five-star experiences for all clients regardless of team member personality or mood.

episode_title: Fire the Chef: How Systems Save Your Client Experience| EPISODE 238
question: How do systems improve client experience beyond efficiency and automation?
transcript_excerpt: Systems create consistency and enable strong service delivery every time. They solve problems faster, support team performance, and give clients confidence by setting clear expectations. Systems protect the client experience by ensuring the same level of service regardless of which team member delivers it or their circumstances on any given day.

episode_title: Fire the Chef: How Systems Save Your Client Experience| EPISODE 238
question: What is the key difference between clients valuing a product versus valuing the experience after delivery?
transcript_excerpt: Most business owners improve their products but neglect the experience they deliver. Clients don't necessarily value the product or service itself—they value what happens after delivery and whether they feel supported. Francesca discovered that her returning clients valued the post-delivery support, communication, and feeling of being looked after more than the core service itself.
